newsitem.title: MALTA: Malaysian to seek bigger stake in Maltaos Lombard.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian to seek bigger stake in Maltaos Lombard.

text.p: The biggest shareholder in Lombard Bank Malta, Malaysian businessman R Tan Hua Choon, has notified the bank that he intends to seek consent to increase his existing shareholding, the bank said.

Hua Choon has a 21.3-percent shareholding and would need the approval from the Malta Stock Exchange, the Central Bank and other shareholders in terms of the bank's articles of association before he can go ahead. He is the only shareholder with more than a five-percent stake in the bank, which the Maltese government privatised in the late 1980s.
Specific details of the proposal are not yet available to the bank, the board of directors said in a statement.
The directors also said they had made progress in establishing strategic alliances with strong overseas partners.

Two foreign financial institutions of standing and repute have expressed interest in developing close business cooperation arrangements. These institutions have also shown interest in acquiring a capital participation in the bank, subject to the necessary approval, the directors said.
But the bank would not give details until the appropriate time, they said.
Lombard is the third largest bank in Malta. Last year, it made an after-tax profit of 368,000 Malta pounds,($957,000) with net interest income increasing by 21 percent over the previous year.
